sentences.text: The second accused in C.C.No.245 of 1998 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Erattupetta filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 50(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Erattupetta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 17.3.1998 at about 2 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased three packets of banana chips, each packet having a weight of 200 gram each, from the shop of the first accused.
The second accused was the licensee of the said shop.
After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.
The Public Analyst filed Ext. P13 report stating that the sample contained synthetic food colour tartarzine and therefore, the same was adulterated under the P.F.A. Rules.

The revision petitioner did not have the required license under the P.F.A. Rules.
4.
Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW5 were examined and Exts. P1 to P26 and X1 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 and DW2 were examined and Exts.D1 to D3 were marked for the revision petitioner.

5. The trial court after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the parties,
acquitted the revision petitioner for the offence of adulteration.

However, the revision petitioner was convicted for the offence under Sections 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 50(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, for violation of the provisions of license.

The Appellate court also found that the revision petitioner did not obtain the P.F.A.
license from the Panchayath.

The courts below concurrently convicted the revision petitioner under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 50(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

Having gone through the relevant inputs, I find no reason to disturb the finding by the courts below that the revision petitioner, who was the owner of the Bakery, from where PW1 purchased the food articles, sold the food articles to PW1 without obtaining license from the competent authority, under the PFA Rules.

Therefore, the concurrent finding by the courts below that the revision petitioner committed the offence under section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 50(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, does not warrant any interference by this Court.
6. As regards the sentence, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has pleaded for leniency.
The revision petitioner was a lady aged 35 years during the relevant time.
Presently, she is aged 51 years.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the sentence in this case can be awarded as provided and the second proviso to Section 16(1) of the P.F.A. Act.

Having regard to the entire facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the sentence awarded Mariamma Kurian vs The Food Inspector on 3 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50325753/
2 by the courts below can be modified and reduced to imprisonment till the rising of the court and a fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees five hundred only) and in default to simple imprisonment for five days under section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 50(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, to secure the ends of justice.

sentences.text: Accordingly I order so.
In the result, this revision petition stands allowed in part as above.
The revision petitioner shall surrender before the trial court on 16.3.2016 to suffer the sentence.
